annotations.text: Structure: left rail (Flows, Runs, Bindings, Agents and tools, API, Data, Settings), centre workspace, right inspector. The eleven tabs are gone; every old screen has a home. Command palette on ⌘K lists the same actions the TUI, SDK and CLI have.
All content is real: the fixtures project, the comp run that compensated, the fake-gateway record decision, the WebMCP binding, the heal of schedule-build-link, the agent invocations from the audit.

yam ui: full authoring cockpit, standalone Ink app over the same service. Four numbered panes, Tab to cycle, ^K palette with the same action list as the app. --json streams the audit pane for agents. Shown: run comp after compensation, palette open on 'heal'.
Dark-first, light theme beside it. Radix primitives, own tokens. One accent (amber), five status colours with words beside them. Every control named and id'd for the desktop adapters.

Draft 2.26 — the terminal owns its view layer. The eight boards to the right are the proposed cockpit, not the shipped one: the alternate screen filled by a solved region tree, a live run driven by the event stream, the palette as an overlay with reasons on unavailable actions, the empty project before and after, the default screen driving a live target with no project, and the cockpit while Yam serves MCP. Parity with the app is every action reachable and --json equal to the model, not the same panes and the same keys. See docs/spec/view-layers/.

Draft 2.27 — Session replaces Surfaces and Record as a destination and becomes the rail's default. The rail drawn here is the one REQ-ADE-11 describes; macros.mjs still draws the pre-2.25 rail on every other board on this page, which is TV-A01. Motion, a tree, a following log and a picker overlay are what packages/ui still owes this design: TV-A03 and TV-A04.
